results.content:
And I fully agree that having stack profile up-to-date is one of the main challenge, that's why there're multiple ways to automate that on Stackness. I also plan to publish skills on GitHub to make it even easier to plug in their setup.

Reading the repo or package file is a nice idea, although I'm worried that many people don't share that stuff publicly and scanning them would be complicated. Their AI tools on the other hand can do that and upload things themself :) I'll give it another thought to make it more convenient, thanks again for the feedback!

Daniel Henry
Premarket Bell

Premarket Bell

The one link stack profile is a really handy idea. It would be nice to share your whole setup without having to list every tool separately.

Sergei Gordeichuk
Stackness

Stackness [...] Asad M.

You asked whether it's relevant. The thing that kills every stack profile site is staleness, because mine would be accurate for about three weeks and then sit there lying about a tool I dropped, and I'm not coming back to edit it. The MCP server is the most interesting thing here and it's the last four words of your description, since that's the one path where the profile updates itself instead of nagging me. I'd make reading a repo or a package file the default way a stack gets built and leave manual entry as the fallback.

Sergei Gordeichuk
Stackness

Hi @asadmalik901 !

Thanks a lot for the feedback, I really appreciate that. I'm totally agree that MCP server feature should be prominent, I'll probably move it higher in all descriptions :) [...] Sergei Gordeichuk

@daniel\_henry4 thanks a lot! initial setup is quite annoying because I had to reflect and analyse what I'm actually using haha but then that gave me idea of the onboarding wizard and also "stack builder" feature which basically allows you to select a bunch of tools by clicking (similar to Spotify), so it might help. And then there's always AI which can scan the projects and extract the tools
